- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot — cap forecast 3–5 days after peak at 10–15% below peak.  
- If sentiment is positive and forecast is low, consider a 3–5 day lagged mean reversion bias — adjust upward by 2–4% per day.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often overestimates mean — apply a 3–7% downward correction for 10-day horizon.  
- If recent history shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops) and sentiment is negative, forecast should be adjusted downward by 5–8% to reflect momentum.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 70% of 30-day average, apply a 5–10% downward bias to avoid overconfidence in short-term recovery.
